Use useLayoutEffect when you need to read or change layout before the browser paints, e.g. measuring an element and then positioning a tooltip, or restoring scroll, so the user never sees the wrong first frame. useEffect runs after paint, so it is the default for everything else (fetching, subscriptions, logging), and useLayoutEffect blocks painting so keep it small. It also warns on the server, so in SSR code guard it or only use it in client-only components.

The flicker comes from replacing the whole table element on every change. Least dumb fix: only swap the rows, e.g. target the tbody with hx-target='#trails tbody' and hx-select='#trails tbody' with hx-swap='outerHTML swap:0ms settle:0ms', so the header and column widths stay put. If it still flashes, the idiomorph extension (hx-swap='morph:outerHTML') diffs the DOM instead of replacing it, at the cost of one extra script.

There is a real difference. structuredClone keeps Dates, Maps, Sets, typed arrays, undefined and circular references, while the JSON round trip turns Dates into strings, Maps and Sets into {}, drops undefined and functions, and throws on cycles. Neither copies functions or class prototypes, and structuredClone is available in Node 17 and later, so it is fine on 18 LTS.

Action: none for now; if you tell me where you plan to use it I can check the data has no functions or class instances.
